title: Integrated MF-C tool — macro-fiscal and climate
subtitle: a fiscal outlook with tax, spending and carbon pricing levers, built from the Global Fiscal Indicators dashboard (v1.3 panel, with the Climate Fiscal Risk Dashboard v1.5 series), the National Mitigation Investment Model (NMIM v0.2), the CDPM-based investment needs workbook (v1.1, cross-check), PriceFeasibility v0.1 (live) and MacroFiscalModels (GIMF / DIGNAD / DIGNAR-lite, LIC-DSF-lite; DIGNAD-R live).

readme_replace.What this is: The integrated macro-fiscal climate (MF-C) tool. Its front page, the Fiscal outlook, is a revenue and expenditure outlook to 2050 for one country: set new taxes, new public investment and other spending, the fiscal rule and power-sector carbon pricing (a carbon tax, a feebate, or the most effective mix that stays within political-feasibility limits), and see what they do to revenue, spending, the balance, debt, growth and green public investment, beside the country's climate programme. Behind it sit the Global Fiscal Indicators dashboard, the mitigation investment needs and the macro-fiscal models: what the net zero programme needs and costs, how much falls on the budget, and whether the country can pay for it, build it and finance it. The is_ccdr column flags the 98 economies with a published Country Climate and Development Report.
readme_replace.How it is organised: Sheets: Fiscal outlook (levers and outlook), Dashboard, Macro (GDP and debt paths, the integrated run beside the live simple model), DSA (debt-sustainability indicators against thresholds), Pricing (carbon tax and feebate options). The Dashboard has sixteen blocks, in reading order. Four ASSESSMENT blocks carry the diagnosis: fiscal space, delivery, cost of capital, and financing. Three CONTEXT blocks explain it: fossil revenue in the budget, fossil trade and extraction, and power generation. Two INVESTMENT blocks give the need: Investment 1 (need by sector, incremental cost under three cost-of-capital lenses, the path to 2050) and Investment 2 (public investment needs: the budget need and who else pays); they read High / Medium / Low, like the Context blocks. Two MACRO blocks give the consequences: Macro 1 (how much of the budget need carbon pricing can pay) and Macro 2 (growth, debt, a cross-check with the other model family, debt-carrying capacity and debt risk); they carry no block verdict, because their rows point different ways. Five APPENDIX blocks are reference detail in grey: fuel pricing, power market regulation, macro-model inputs (including the debt-sustainability inputs), fiscal risk, and a cross-check of the investment need with the CDPM-based method.
readme_replace.Appendix C and D: Appendix C holds what the macro-fiscal models start from: WEO ratios, public investment (IMF ICSD, to 2019; used by the models), and the debt-sustainability inputs - external public debt and its share of all public debt (IDS; used by LIC-DSF-lite), the concessional share, CPIA, remittances and reserves (used for debt-carrying capacity) - with account ownership (Findex) as a candidate proxy for hand-to-mouth households (not yet used). The dashboard's Appendix D (the integrated scenario) is replaced here by the Macro 1 and Macro 2 blocks and the Macro and DSA sheets.
readme_replace.How to use it: Fiscal outlook: pick a country in the yellow cell at the top; every sheet follows it. Change the yellow levers: new taxes (pp of GDP added each year, up to a ceiling), new public investment and other spending (pp of GDP at full scale), the fiscal rule, and carbon pricing (mode, limits, phase-in, revenue use). The table and charts recalculate: policy scenario by revenue and spending item, the no-new-measures baseline, and the difference. Pricing: the feasible tax and feebate mixes and a grid of abatement, green where all limits hold. Dashboard: the same country. Everything resolves - evaluation, score, value, observation year, coverage - grouped and coloured by block. Macro: the same country's GDP and debt paths - the integrated run, the other model family as a cross-check, and the live simple model - with charts; Macro_assumptions holds the simple model's yellow assumptions, including p_programme (the climate programme on or off) and the carbon pricing priors. DSA: the five LIC-DSF-lite indicators against their thresholds, before and with the programme. Data_wide is the cross-section, Data_long names the source file for every value, Scores holds the 1-10 rescaling, Spec is the indicator list, Sources lists the datasets.

readme_add: Investment 1 and 2 are MODEL OUTPUT, not data, from the National Mitigation Investment Model (InvestmentNeeds/national_model/, NMIM v0.2): 186 countries, 2024-2050, baseline and net zero, 2024 prices, built bottom-up from energy, power and emissions stocks. The same model feeds the macro-fiscal run in Appendix D. Values are % of NMIM's GDP for the year; the year column is the scenario year. See InvestmentNeeds/national_model/NMIM_Method_v0_2.md.

Incremental = net zero less the current-trends baseline. Incremental cost = annual capital charge on the incremental capital in service less fuel and operating savings (lens c also less local co-benefits); negative = net saving. Lens (a) uses the market WACC, (b) and (c) the World Bank 6% rate; the cost-of-capital penalty is (a) less (b), negative where market capital is cheaper than 6%.

NMIM splits all net zero investment by who repays it: P1 pure public (taxes), P2 regulated utility (tariffs), P3 contracted revenue (a public or regulated buyer), P4 viability gap (private with a public top-up), P5 pure private. Three public measures, narrow to wide: the direct budget need (P1 + the public 30% of P4: money the budget spends); plus regulated utilities (adds P2, a contingent liability where tariffs do not recover costs); and all investment needing public money or a public decision (P1 + P2 + all of P4). The PIMA-adjusted budget need divides the budget need by (1 - efficiency gap): the gap is mapped from PEFA PI-11 where the dashboard has it (40% at 1 to 13% at 4), else IMF (2015) income-group gaps (AE 13%, low income 40%, others 27%). Private capital is P3 + P5 + the other 70% of P4. The type shares are judgements applied to country data, not observed splits; power market structure rests on PSRT data that end in 2013.

Macro 1 and 2 are MODEL OUTPUT from the MacroFiscalModels integrated run, pre-computed in Python for 186 countries: dashboard -> NMIM (budget need) -> PriceFeasibility (feasible power-sector carbon pricing, revenue earmarked for the need) -> one macro model per country (GIMF-lite for most upper-middle and high-income countries, DIGNAD-lite for low-income and concessional borrowers, DIGNAR-lite where fossil rents are 10% of GDP or more) -> LIC-DSF-lite (low and lower-middle income only). The cross-check rows run the other model family on the same programme (DIGNAD-lite where GIMF-lite was chosen, GIMF-lite otherwise; GIMF-lite has no resource block). Debt-carrying capacity comes from the Composite Indicator where the dashboard has a CPIA score (IDA countries), medium otherwise; exports and imports are still assumptions. 'Today's path' is GDP with no trend growth from 2024; the baseline is the same model with no programme. Calibrations are illustrative.

The Macro sheet adds DIGNAD-R: DIGNAD-lite / DIGNAR-lite made recursive and written in formulas (MacroFiscalModels/ExcelDIGNAD), for the country picked on the Dashboard. Change the yellow cells on Macro_assumptions - disaster year, grant and concessional shares, pricing earmark, fiscal-rule speed - and it recalculates. It is DIGNAD-type for every country, has one fiscal instrument and no energy savings, so it differs from the integrated run, most for GIMF-lite countries and where the fiscal rule had to tighten.

Appendix E: fiscal risk from the World Bank Climate Fiscal Risk Dashboard v1.5 (ratings, rollover, external and short-term debt; climate in public investment management, budget tagging, a national climate fund). Appendix F: the same country's 2030 need from the CDPM-based global method (the v1.1 workbook: IHLEG and IEA-IFC group totals allocated to countries, with one public share per country group), as a cross-check on NMIM; the two will not match.
Fiscal outlook: what the numbers are

Computed live by DIGNAD-R, the recursive DIGNAD-lite / DIGNAR-lite of the Macro sheet, for the 186 countries of the integrated run. It has no trend growth: the baseline holds the 2024 position (revenue, spending and debt ratios) except that fossil rents fall, and growth is shown above or below trend. Use it to compare packages, not as a forecast. Carbon pricing is PriceFeasibility v0.1 (power sector only; several parameters are priors, not country evidence). The integrated run on the Macro sheet is pre-computed and does not respond to the levers.
